note: Project-only status, newest first. This page replaces routine chat reports. It is edited by hand when the project changes; nothing here is a live feed, and it does not claim live, unattended or independently verified operation.

items.title: WP4: acceptance-flow mechanics demonstrated with scripted seats; real re-proof stays model-blocked
items.body: A scripted-seat demonstration of the WP4 acceptance flow ran unattended on the accepted pin a1c36ce: one batch through the real launcher supervisor - builder change, Reviewer turn, QC verdict, guarded close, zero gates or manual recovery, and the application bytes identical between the QC verdict head and the final head. Script and result record are on branch live/wp4-reproof at 31c01c9 (https://github.com/coolkowkank/Multiple-Human-Concept-Owner/commit/31c01c9128083ea7f978b222a4722a3dda34f9ff), not integrated. Independent review re-ran it fresh (all flow checks true) but judged it is NOT a WP4 re-proof: every seat's output is predetermined queued text, the Reviewer's verdict names no pin, and no negative path ran - so it earns no WP4 credit and shows flow mechanics only, not review judgment, model ability or autonomy. WP4's real qualification (Reviewer and QC judgment on the same application pin, unattended) stays blocked on a model-backed route, which needs its own grounding and authority before any use.

items.title: Reviewer-skip acceptance guard accepted and published on the execution line
items.body: The Reviewer-skip acceptance guard needed by WP4 and WP10 is accepted after three review rounds and published as the reviewed code on the execution line: live/operator-done fast-forwarded 5e140fc to a1c36ce (https://github.com/coolkowkank/Multiple-Human-Concept-Owner/commit/a1c36ced14708b3c032d580ea83d6dcc32d547f0), 4 commits, identical tree to the reviewed pin, no merge, no force, no activation. What the guard does: a DONE claim closes only with a fresh QC PASS verdict in the bus - the whole-line bare 'PASS'/'QC PASS' form, optionally 'at head <sha>' bound to the real head; without one the turn routes to a QC seat, or parks on a human gate when the roster has none. A QC turn may close on its own earlier PASS only with the bare word DONE; any other QC DONE text records a vetoing verdict. Evidence, stated with its scope: 44 focused guard checks pass, the full 32-file offline suite passes serially, and the self-checking demo closes end to end - all author-run in one sandbox, offline. An independent reviewer probed each round offline and ACCEPTed this pin scoped to the guard (own-writes refusal, rename/space-safe freshness, newest-verdict-wins, whole-line PASS grammar, QC DONE veto, binding head claim); a parallel product probe found no distinct defect on the final delta. Neither reviewer ran the suite; the scripted endurance example passed at the previous round's code and was not rerun on the final pin (its verdict lines carry no head claim, so the round-4 change cannot affect it). Limits carried: verdict rows are cooperative .team records - they show a QC-role seat's turn recorded the row, not identity beyond the roster role claim; QC self-close on an earlier fresh PASS is a stated policy; freshness is the ancestor-plus-evidence-paths rule, a deliberate narrowing of the spec's 'current head' text; with no QC seat the DONE claim parks on a human gate and the operator sets a turn by hand. This is not a WP10 completion and not an autonomy claim. Next: the WP4 re-proof with Reviewer and QC on this pin, run through the actual existing launcher workflow.

items.title: Next step chosen: Reviewer-skip acceptance guard (WP4/WP10), third draft in review
items.body: Of the two recorded candidates, the guard came first: batch 7 closed failed with the independent reviewer never asked (record 35b0a3c), the guard blocks both the WP4 re-proof and WP10 (weight 23), and WP9's request-ID join already exists (launcher/usage_join.py) while its matched savings comparison stays blocked on provider composition - so WP9 could not advance regardless. The guard is on branch live/wp10-reviewer-skip-guard, two commits on the execution line 5e140fc. First draft 29d6ca5 was reviewed offline and rejected with three reproduced bypasses (a DONE turn's own application writes slipped past the verdict, free-text PASS parsing accepted negations like 'QC cannot PASS this build', and a rename could hide application work) plus a prefix-normalization hole; the corrected 7f214b0 closed those and made a newer QC FAIL cancel an older PASS. A second review round then rejected 7f214b0 on two more reproduced holes: the PASS parser was a blacklist, not a grammar (a qualified line like 'PASS (2 tests fail)' or 'PASS if the owner agrees' still recorded PASS), and a QC turn saying 'DONE FAIL' or 'DONE - found a blocking bug' could close the cycle on its own earlier PASS. Both are fixed in the current head 1da5b46 (https://github.com/coolkowkank/Multiple-Human-Concept-Owner/commit/1da5b462497417c61ee8cd64d2b194f10d4725b7): only the whole-line bare PASS or QC PASS form counts as a pass, and only a bare-word QC DONE may close on an earlier verdict. A QC turn now records a machine-checkable verdict row (PASS/FAIL plus the head it rules on). A DONE claim closes only with a fresh QC PASS verdict - fresh means no application work was committed after the verdict, with review and archive paths counted as evidence, not work. Without it the DONE is refused: the turn routes to a QC seat and a review-required row names the claimant, and when the roster has no QC seat a human gate opens and the turn parks. A refused DONE never records a DONE status_line. Evidence: 40 focused checks pass (the 14 new ones fail on the previously rejected runtime as mutation), the full 32-file offline suite passes serially, and the self-checking demo and the scripted endurance example both close end to end - all author-run in one sandbox, offline. Independent reviews of 1da5b46 are pending, so it is not accepted and not a rollout. No model calls, no provider or account changes.

items.title: Coordination bus fix: reviewed offline and integrated, execution line now 5e140fc
items.body: Reading the code showed that the LangGraph coordination bus (execution line, then d4a7485) could drop a commit that did land: if a push errors and the remote then cannot be read, it reset its commit and retried, which could repeat a batch of work. Reproduced offline in disposable local repositories (6 checks fail on the old code). The fix keeps the commit and stops with a distinct error when the remote cannot be read, with no reset and no retry; retry stays only when every push destination was read and provably lacks the commit. The operator callers handle the unknown case: a gate answer or lease release is reported as committed locally with the push outcome unknown, and a seat stops with its own exit code so the supervisor does not restart and replay it. An end-to-end lifecycle probe with real seat subprocesses and disposable local remotes showed a later supervisor poll neither restarts nor replays a stopped seat. Reviews, all offline and of exact commits: an independent reviewer accepted the source changes (running the 18 tri-state and 12 destination checks itself), accepted the lifecycle probe as substantive evidence (running its 18 checks itself), and accepted the integrated staging commit 5e140fc (https://github.com/coolkowkank/Multiple-Human-Concept-Owner/commit/5e140fc1bfa0d80cbb01a4ae3727c72a8aa29c85) on identity and provenance (same tree as the reviewed branch). The full 31-file offline suite was run by the author only, in one sandbox; the reviewer did not repeat it. After the final accept, the execution line moved from d4a7485 to 5e140fc, a fast-forward with nothing else changed. Limits kept: an absence reading is only true at read time, so the documented at-least-once retry stays; late server completion and remote rewinds are not covered; the bus is not exactly-once; a spending seat that stops this way gets only a console line and a local escalation gate; a relaunch from another clone is untested; the reviews are same-model-family. This is an offline reviewed code change only: no live run, rollout, or activation. Unchanged: the runtime does not contain or call the push-gate executor, so nothing is integrated there and no integration progress is claimed.

items.title: Push gate: race found and fixed on a review branch, reviewed offline
items.body: An independent offline review of the push gate found a real race: the gate approved one commit, a concurrent writer then moved HEAD, and the push published the unapproved commit. A fix is on branch live/gate-push-binding at 4f77e2f (https://github.com/coolkowkank/Multiple-Human-Concept-Owner/commit/4f77e2fd0c1981072af0de39675e443f17263ef8). It pushes the exact approved commit, never forced, and then checks every push destination for exactly that commit. A product-side adversarial check also found and closed two false-success cases in that check (a look-alike branch name and a separate push URL). A failed or partly failed push is reported as possibly published or unverified, never as unpublished, and is never retried. The final review found no defect in this scope. Verified offline only. Limits: the check reads the branch tip once and is not atomic; it assumes a single writer; file-system and symlink trust are unchanged; no real remote, provider or account was used. Three code lines now exist and they are separate: execution code d4a7485 (live/operator-done), handover code f92cf45 (live/handover-portability), and the ledger and gate work built on 61ca8c9 and 4f77e2f. The gate fix is not rolled into the runtime. WP6 stays partial with no credit change; the Reviewer-skip guard is still unbuilt and WP10 is untouched.

items.title: Budget ledger and pacing: scoped review complete, no blockers
items.body: Integration 61ca8c9 (module aacfe44, base 4a95bf5) was independently reviewed offline and the reviewer found no blockers: https://github.com/coolkowkank/Multiple-Human-Concept-Owner/commit/61ca8c9e141c326059e214a331cf2f6a7893e620 . Seven scoped behaviors were verified: atomic write, validated counts, concurrent exact cap, pacing re-check under the lock, missing or corrupt ledger fails closed with no reset, halt before any send on ledger errors, ambiguous completion stays consumed. The reviewer reran 256 tests, 10 integration and 39 ledger tests, and 150 real process-kill probes. Non-blocking backlog: import-path trust, a symlink check race, conservative error masking, never-started reservations consuming cap, no automatic legacy migration. Limits: offline and process-crash only. Not tested: live provider, runtime or real-time pacing, security, power loss, NFS. No rollout. The review did not cover the push-gate fingerprint, so WP6 stays partial with no credit change. The Reviewer-skip guard is still unbuilt and WP10 is untouched.

items.title: Verifier qualification test failed
items.body: One request was sent to the free route for the verifier model. The provider answered HTTP 404 and returned no verdict. It was not retried, no other role ran, and Ryan's review did not run. As recorded privately at 15:01, the runner is paused by its own halt record, and that test window is stopped. Cause is unknown: the model is listed as free but was not callable as requested. This is not a model-quality result. The full team is not autonomous. No model or role is qualified.

items.body: Read-only checks of public documentation found no verifier route that is both callable and independent. One other candidate has unresolved upstream terms and another has no evidenced output ceiling, so neither is qualified. One request remains in each of the runner and shared request limits (counted separately), which is not enough for a verifier plus Ryan's review. Next: pick a callable, independent route through a reviewed change. No requests, limits or assignments were changed.

items.title: Handover tooling built and tested offline
items.body: Added a setup guide (HANDOVER.md), a read-only environment and state checker (31 passing checks) and a fresh-environment script. The script clones the repository, builds a new virtual environment with the pinned packages, scrubs the environment and runs all 29 test files: all exit 0 with no network request. This was tested in one sandbox only, not on another machine or with another AI operator, so the handover is not yet proven end to end. Secrets stay out of Git and nothing transfers from the previous operator's accounts; a new operator supplies their own keys. The previous operator's chat history and prompts are not exported. Private run records go over only by a separate private route, if at all. Nothing has been transferred to anyone.

items.title: Known test environment dependency
items.body: live_entry_test.py fails 6 checks when HOME is not the account home, because the reserve preflight guard refuses a different HOME. With the right HOME it passes 57 of 57. The test was not edited; the guide states the requirement.

items.body: The public branch holds code and tests. The latest run records, including the failed verifier test and the paused runner, are in a private runner folder and are not in Git. A new operator reads that state with the read-only state checker, and does not reset it: a halt or unknown outcome stands.
